prerequisites: Laplace transform and frequency response as fundamental tools for the analysis and synthesis of control loops.

learning_outcomes.text: Graduates have a broad overview of frequency and time domain methods and can apply these techniques to complex systems.
Graduates can compare important methods for systems with concentrated parameters in specific technical applications and implement them for complex systems.
Graduates possess broad knowledge of control engineering and are particularly able to communicate with users at the interfaces to the process or information processing.

syllabus_topics: Complex control systems (controllers with two degrees of freedom, disturbance feedforward, anti-windup, cascade control, ...)
Sampled-data control (discrete analysis and synthesis, z-transformation)
Outlook on modern control engineering methods
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is an exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 6 experiments, each lasting 90 minutes. Exam duration is according to the valid study regulations.
bibliography: K. J. Astom, M. Murray: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers. Princeton University Press. 2021.
M. Horn, N. Dourdoumas: Regelungstechnik. Pearson. 2004.
